summary: Sonoma County's Mount Jackson lookout opened in 1928, was staffed into 1939 and was intentionally burned in 1995; no recent description of the site was found.

facts.status_note: Intentionally burned in 1995. The latest site note, from 1991, lists communications structures and a water tank.

access.note: Not accessible to the public; the lookout lies about a mile behind a locked gate, per a 1991 register note.

corrections.why: The register says the summit first hosted a lookout in 1928, and the 809R-type construction dates to 1947. The register's built field reads 1948, so the record's single 1948 entry leaves out the 1928 structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's built field reads 1948, but its text gives 1928 for the first lookout and 1947 for the oldest 809R-type construction. The story gives 1928 for the first lookout and 1947 for the surviving building type, and mentions the 1948 field.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. Today's condition rests on the register's 1991 site note (MVT 10/91); nothing later was found, and the Sonoma County Library record has no text. The Water Boards PDF on the Mount Jackson mercury mine was not used for the lookout: it concerns the mine site off Sweetwater Springs Road. Staffing evidence runs from 1929 to 1939 in the newspaper transcripts; no later staffing was found. The register's built field (1948) disagrees with its own description (1928 first lookout, 1947 oldest construction); the story follows the description and mentions the field.
